_why: Mutant ids declared BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING for ExtController, each with the reason. `vit_mutate.py --equivalences` reads the KEYS of this object (json.loads then set(...)), so the reasons live in the same file as the claim. A declared equivalence leaves the denominator, so each one is a claim that has to be answerable. EACH OF THESE FOUR WAS APPLIED BY HAND AND RE-RUN before it was declared -- 'it survived' is a measurement here, not an inference from the batch -- and each is UNOBSERVABLE rather than equivalent-by-the-standard: the mutated quantity is real, and no input in the admissible domain can carry it to an output. That distinction is stated rather than smoothed over.
11d2c9cc: compare_op '<=' -> '<' at `if (len_new <= (int)ErrVar->n_ErrMsg_cap)`. Applied by hand: 163 checked, 0 failed. The two forms differ only at len_new == n_ErrMsg_cap. len_new is 14 in every case that reaches the branch (13 for 'ExtController', 1 for ':', and LEN_TRIM(ErrVar%ErrMsg) is 0 -- see 227f7621), while n_ErrMsg_cap is the harness's buffer, LEN(ErrMsg) + harness.emit.ALLOC_HEADROOM = 3 + 4096. NOT REMOVED: the guard is what makes an over-long assignment a REFUSAL rather than a truncation, and a truncated error message is the one wrong answer a bit comparison cannot catch. Deleting it to raise the score would delete the property.
227f7621: arith_op `ErrVar->ErrMsg + len_RoutineName` -> `- len_RoutineName`, the memmove destination. Applied by hand: 163 checked, 0 failed. The memmove moves `lt` bytes and lt is LEN_TRIM(ErrVar%ErrMsg) AFTER LoadDynamicLib, whose first statement is `ErrMsg = ''` on a `CHARACTER(*), INTENT(OUT)` dummy (SysGnuLinux.f90:78) -- blank-filling the whole declared length. So lt is 0 on every path that returns, and a memmove of zero bytes has no destination to get wrong. NOT REMOVED: `TRIM(ErrVar%ErrMsg)` is in the original and restates nothing. It is constant only because harness/ranges.toml pins LocalVar_iStatus to 0, which runs LoadDynamicLib on every case; with iStatus /= 0 the caller's message survives and lt can be non-zero. That pin is a property of the harness, not of the function.
4193a767: const_tweak '1' -> '2'. One of the pair below; the mutator's ids carry no line, so the two are declared as a pair rather than matched individually -- stated rather than guessed. Both sites were applied by hand and both survived 163 cases.
75897666: const_tweak '1' -> '2'. The pair is (a) `std::vector<char> avcMSG((size_t)len_ErrMsg + 1)` -> `+ 2` and (b) `std::memmove(ErrVar->ErrMsg + len_RoutineName + 1, ...)` -> `+ 2`. (a) avcMSG's SIZE is read by nothing: the buffer is a local, discarded after the call, and the external library is told how many bytes it may use by RECORD 49, which is LEN(avcMSG) + 1 = 2 and does not come from the array bound (evidence/ExtController/len_probe.txt). (b) is 227f7621's reason -- it moves zero bytes. NOT REMOVED: `avcMSG(LEN(ErrVar%ErrMsg)+1)` is the original's declaration and appears once already.
_not_declared: FOUR OTHER MUTANTS SURVIVED THE FIRST PASS AND ARE NOT HERE, because they were not equivalent -- they were RESTATEMENTS, and were removed from the translation instead. `accINFILE`'s bound and record 50 are both `LEN_TRIM(DLL_InFile)+1`, and `avcOUTNAME`'s bound and record 51 are both `LEN_TRIM(ExtRootName)+1`; transcribing each twice left a second site computing a quantity nothing reads back. Naming each once (`n_accINFILE`, `n_avcOUTNAME`) leaves only the observable site. The two explicit NUL terminators went the same way: the vectors are zero-initialised, so writing the terminator again set a byte the initialiser had already set. That is the third time in this campaign that removing a restatement raised a mutation score -- unit #1 named a SIZE once, unit #4 a LOOP BOUND, and this a BUFFER LENGTH.
_and_one_was_fixed_in_the_fixture: A fifth survivor, `int aviFAIL = 0;` -> `= 1`, was neither declared nor removed: the ORACLE was changed so the value became observable. `aviFAIL` is a local that ExtController zeroes, passes to the external library and never reads again, so the assignment was write-only and unkillable. The stub now reports the INCOMING value back in record 44 before overwriting it (`fixtures/bladed_stub/discon_stub.c`, REC_OUT_E), and the mutant is killed on all 163 cases. Where a blindness is in the instrument rather than in the unit, the instrument is what to change.
